PREAMBLE.TITLE: Preamble
PREAMBLE.CONTENT: The CodinGame Contests are online programming competitions where programmers / software developers from around the world (the “Participants”) come to challenge themselves for fun, or to showcase their skills (the “CodinGame Contests”). {br} CodinGame Contests involve the development of computer programs using one of the offered programming languages to solve complex problems within a limited time frame. These contests are anonymous, and no personal data is shared with CodinGame's potential partners.

ART1.TITLE: Article 1: Organization of the CodinGame Contests
ART1.CONTENT: CodinGame, is owned by CoderPad France SA, registered with the Trade and Companies Register of Montpellier (France) under the number 75053861300019, whose headquarters are located at 396 rue du Mas de Verchant, Immeuble Archimède - 34000 Montpellier, France, organizes the CodinGame programming Contests.{br}{br}CodinGame Contests take place online on the Internet (or, in some cases, online and onsite) at dates (and locations) specified on the Site <cgLink>www.codingame.com</cgLink> (the “Site”).{br}{br}CodinGame Contests are anonymous for all Participants. No personal data are shared with any partner.

ART2.TITLE: Article 2: Conditions for participating in the CodinGame Contests
ART2.CONTENT:
Detailed information on the CodinGame Contests and how to participate can be found on the Site: www.codingame.com.{br}{br}CodinGame Contests are open to any individual over 18 years old, with an internet connection and a valid email address, regardless of their nationality, and without any specific educational or professional requirements.{br}{br}Configuration requirements to participate to CodinGame Contests are as follows: access to the Internet, a valid email address, and a valid postal address.{br}{br}Participant undertakes to participate to CodinGame Contests using equipment that meets the configuration requirements described above, and that does not contain any viruses.{br}{br}Access to the CodinGame Contests is prohibited for the following people:{br}{br}
  • Officers and employees of CodinGame or any CodinGame affiliate (i.e. company it controls, which controls it or under common control with it), as well as their family members (ascendants and descendants);
  • Anyone who has worked or is working on developing the CodinGame Contests, as well as their family members (direct ascendants and descendants).
{br}CodinGame reserves the right to ask any Participant to justify these conditions. Any Participant who doesn't meet these conditions or who refuses to provide proof shall be excluded from the CodinGame Contest and shall not benefit from the advantages if successful in the CodinGame Contest.{br}{br}By participating in a CodinGame Contest, all Participants shall act in a fair and loyal manner and refrain from cheating, faking, thieving identity or any other technique to change the result of the Contest. They shall be required to participate and perform tests alone without the help of a third party or any technical assistance.{br}{br}Participation in the CodinGame Contests is free of charge for Participants and doesn't imply any purchase obligation.{br}{br}Participation is strictly personal ; each Participant may only register once for a particular CodinGame Contest and may not participate in any way on behalf of third parties.{br}{br}As such, Participant acknowledges that their access to the Site and CodinGame Contests is strictly personal and confidential. Participant is forbidden to make these accesses available to third parties, whether free of charge or in return for payment.{br}{br}Participant is responsible for the management and security of the accesses they have received, and is required to notify CodinGame of any compromise of his identifiers or unauthorized access to the Site.{br}{br}The Participants irrevocably agree that all solutions that they submit to the CodinGame platform during the Contest (the “Solutions”) may be published under the open source GPL v3 license, that they shall transfer all corresponding intellectual property rights according to the conditions of such licence and that all abovementioned solutions may be made ​​publicly available to anyone through CodinGame at the end of the Contest, under the conditions detailed in the GPL v3 license.{br}However Participants retain ownership of all intellectual and industrial property rights (including moral rights) in and to code they submit to the CodinGame platform during the Contest.{br}{br}Participation in the CodinGame Contests implies acceptance of these in their entirety. Failure to comply with these shall result in the participation being considered null and void.{br}{br}Participants also state that they submit to the decisions of CodinGame for any case not provided for in these or any contentious situation.{br}

ART3.TITLE: Article 3: Conditions for Registering for the CodinGame Contests
ART3.CONTENT:
To participate in a CodinGame Contest, Participants simply need to connect to the Site, click on the button "Join in" corresponding to the selected CodinGame Contest, and register by filling in the following fields:{br}{br}
  • email
  • password
  • nickname
{br}Additional information may be requested but is not required for registration.{br}{br}To become familiar with the development platform used for the CodinGame Contests, Participants can access a training page on the Site by clicking on the following link: GAMES.

ART4.TITLE: Article 4: Practical programming test
ART4.CONTENT: At the date and time the CodinGame Contest starts, registered Participants will receive a link at the email address indicated when registering to the Contest, through which they will be able to connect to the Contest platform.{br}{br}The platform provides an online development environment that allows Participants to solve the Contest's programming problems and submit their program directly online, without having to resort to external programs.{br}{br}Participants may choose to use their own development environment but they then must submit their response within the online development environment for the answer to be taken into account by the rating system (an illustrative example of this is on the Site).{br}{br}Once on the platform, and after having clicked on the "Start" button, Participants shall have access to the first problem statement.{br}{br}Participants have an overall time to finish the Contest. This time is noted at the top of the IDE, it counts down and ends at the same time for everyone. Within that timeframe, Participants can manage the time they spend on each problem as they wish.{br}{br}In order to facilitate time management, an indicative duration to solve each problem is displayed on top of each exercise statement. Participants can navigate through the questions, choose to spend more time on a problem, or go back to a previous question to refine their solution until the overall time is elapsed.{br}{br}However, on the last question, once the "Submit" button has been clicked, the total work is considered validated and Participants cannot go back to modify their programs anymore. If Participants have not submitted their solutions on the platform within the overall time limit, their work will be submitted automatically as is.

ART5.TITLE: Article 5: Determination of result
ART5.CONTENT:
The evaluation of Participants is objective and is done on the platform through an automated system configured in order to evaluate the solutions submitted by Participants.{br}{br}Code submitted by Participants for each question will be compiled and evaluated according to the following criteria:{br}{br}
    Scores for the test cases
{br}Points are awarded when the solution is sent to the platform: the code is tested with test cases that reflect the specifications associated with the problem statement. In order to avoid cheating, these test cases are different from those given in the problem statement.{br}{br}Participants whose code passes all test cases on the platform servers shall obtain the maximum score.{br}{br}Applicants whose code does not compile or fails all the test cases will be assigned a score of zero. {br}Participants' codes are evaluated on a set of test cases directly related to the statement of each problem. {br}On the basis of this automatic evaluation, each Participant will receive a score calculated using the following formula: sum of points for each test passed / total sum of all the test cases. {br}This ratio is expressed in the form of a percentage.{br}{br}
    Submission time
{br}In the case of tied scores, Participants may be ranked taking into account the time taken to submit solutions to problems.{br}{br}The time spent to solve a problem shall be considered when deciding between two equal scores: if the number of points awarded to two people is equal then the person who has spent the least time to answer all the problems shall be classified above the other, although the scores remain equal.{br}{br}
    Participants results
{br}The day following the Contest, all Participants will receive by email their detailed results, including the following:{br}
  • Their score
  • The source code of their solutions
  • Time spent solving each problem
  • Success or failure of the test cases defined for each problem
  • The number of points associated with each test case
{br}The results are obtained by applying objective criteria, on validation of an automated performance measurement process and the scores and ranking cannot be disputed nor appealed.

ART6.TITLE: Article 6: Rewards - Prizes
ART6.CONTENT: Without any obligation for CodinGame, certain CodinGame Contests may propose rewards in the form of prizes, which may be given to Participant(s) with the highest rank.{br}{br}In that case, the description of the CodinGame Contest on the Site will expressly state the awarding (or not) of prizes for the considered CodinGame Contest, which is neither an essential element, nor the primary purpose of the CodinGame Contests.{br}{br}In the event that the CodinGame Contest provides prizes, the description of the CodinGame Contest concerned on the Site will mention the nature of the prizes to be awarded.{br}{br}The Participant who has won an award shall be contacted by email within 2 weeks after the end of the CodinGame Contest and the prize will be sent to the address indicated in the application form. If the Participant does not provide CodinGame with his/her postal address within 7 days after the sending of such email, CodinGame may decide to award the prize to other Participants (following the ranking).{br}{br}Prizes offered may not give rise to any dispute, nor delivery of their exchange value in any form whatsoever, or their replacement or exchange for any causes whatsoever, since this Contest does not constitute a promotional game.{br}{br}CodinGame however, reserves the right to replace prizes with a prize of equal or greater value including, but without limitation, in the event of force majeure, if prizes originally planned are out of stock or in case of any other unforeseen, irresistible and external event which makes it impossible to issue the planned prizes in a timely manner.

ART7.TITLE: Article 7: Data Protection
ART7.CONTENT: The information required on the Site, such as email, name, address, etc... is collected and used in order to manage the Contest, to run a service in accordance with the Participant's expectations, to contact the Participants, to manage the platform, and to keep a record of exchanges and transactions.{br}{br}This information, as well as the information entered in the detailed profile will also be used to generate internal statistics.{br} The technical service providers who may be in charge of the management of the Contest are required to respect the confidentiality of the information and to use it only for the specific operation for which they are required to intervene.{br}{br}Participants have the right to access, rectify or delete their personal information which may be exercised by a simple written request addressed to CodinGame's registered office.{br}{br} For more information concerning your rights, the purposes and legal bases of the processing and the duration of storage of your Data, you may consult our <privacyPolicyLink>Privacy Policy</privacyPolicyLink>.

ART8.TITLE: Article 8: Exclusion
ART8.CONTENT:
Non-compliance with any provision of the items listed above shall lead to disqualification from the CodinGame Contest. The decision shall be made unilaterally by CodinGame.{br}{br}Cheating is forbidden, under penalty of disqualification from the CodinGame Contest. Cheating means:{br}
  • Public release of a solution
  • Exploitation of a flaw in the computing system
  • The use or misuse of a solution
  • An attempt to attack CodinGame servers
  • Obfuscating your code as well as creating obstacles to its reading and understanding.
  • Cheating or wrongdoing observed, such as in particular being assisted by a person or a machine, participating collectively, replacing on behalf of a registered Participant
{br}CodinGame reserves the right to make all the necessary checks regarding the Participants' identity, email and IP address, and generally regarding the respect of the abovementioned rules. {br}Any indication of false identity or email or IP address shall cause the Participant to be eliminated. {br}CodinGame may cancel the participation of any Participant who has not complied with these. {br}This cancellation may be made at any time without notice.

submission_ranking_api_excerpt:
### POST /challenges/{public_id}/submissions

Scope `challenge:submit`. Registered, ongoing. Submits the code to the arena: it replaces the
user's current submission and starts its ranking games. The submission shows in the history of the
user's IDE, with its battles; the code in the IDE does not change.

Body: `{"language": "Python3", "code": "..."}`.

201:

```json
{"submission_id": 321, "progress_url": "/api/v1/challenges/spring-challenge-2026/progress", "limits": {...}}
```

Headers: `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` over the submit windows. 429 `rate-limited` when a window
is exhausted. 400 `INVALID_LANGUAGE`.

### GET /challenges/{public_id}/submissions

Registered, started.

```json
{"submissions": [{"submission_id": 321, "language": "Python3", "submitted_at": "2026-10-05T12:00:00Z", "current": true}]}
```

Newest first. `current` is `true` on the submission playing the ranking games (in optimization
puzzles: the last submission), absent on the others.

### GET /challenges/{public_id}/submissions/{submission_id}

Registered, started.

```json
{"submission_id": 321, "language": "Python3", "current": true, "code": "..."}
```

404 `SUBMISSION_NOT_FOUND`.

### GET /challenges/{public_id}/progress

Registered, started. Ranking of the current submission.

```json
{
  "submission_id": 321,
  "language": "Python3",
  "in_progress": true,
  "percentage": 37,
  "score": 25.5,
  "rank": 120,
  "total": 3500,
  "league": "Bronze",
  "league_rank": 12,
  "league_total": 400,
  "eligible_for_promotion": false,
  "next_promotion_in_seconds": 1234,
  "league_boss": {"name": "Boss 3", "rank": 9, "score": 24.1, "agent_id": 789},
  "league_history": [{"league": "Wood 1", "entered_at": "2026-10-01T15:02:00Z"},
                     {"league": "Bronze", "entered_at": "2026-10-02T09:00:00Z"}],
  "promotion_mode": "rank_above_boss",
  "limits": {...}
}
```

- `percentage`: share of the ranking games played for the current submission; `rank` and `score` move
  until it reaches 100.
- `in_progress`: the ranking games are still being played.
- `league_*`, `eligible_for_promotion` and `next_promotion_in_seconds` exist in challenges with
  leagues. Players above the league boss are promoted when the promotion runs. `league_total`
  counts the boss.
- `league_boss`: the boss of the user's league, with its `rank` and `score` in the league. The
  leaderboard does not list bosses. Test against it with the opponent `boss`.
- `league_history`: the leagues the user entered, oldest first: the league where they joined the
  challenge, then one entry per promotion, with its date in `entered_at`. The last entry is the
  current `league`.
- `promotion_mode`: how the user gets out of their league. Absent when the league has no boss (top
  league, or a league whose next one is not open yet).
  - `rank_above_boss`: the submission becomes `eligible_for_promotion` once it has played all its
    ranking games and its score reaches the boss's; eligible players move up at the next promotion
    run (`next_promotion_in_seconds`).
  - `boss_battles`: each submission plays a series of battles against the boss only, and becomes
    eligible once it wins `boss_battle_wins_required` games outright (alone in first place). The
    league rank does not matter.
- `next_league_opens_at`: in a league without boss, when a boss is scheduled to be added to it,
  which opens the next league. Until then nobody in the league can be promoted.
- Details on each system: [leagues and promotion](https://www.codingame.com/api/v1/docs/leagues).
- Members without a value are absent.

Headers: `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` over all windows. When the leaderboard of the challenge
is hidden, this answers `request-rejected`.

### GET /challenges/{public_id}/leaderboard

| Query | Description |
|---|---|
| `country` | Two-letter country code, e.g. `FR`. |
| `language` | Language, as in the rows' `language`. |
| `league` | `legend`, `gold`, `silver`, `bronze`, `wood`, or `wood` followed by its number (`wood2`). |
| `keyword` | Part of a nickname. |
| `around_me` | `true`: the players around the user (`true` or `false`). |
| `offset` | 0 to 999 (default 0). |
| `limit` | 1 to 100 (default 20). |

At most one filter among `country`, `language`, `league`, `keyword` and `around_me`. A league the
contest does not have answers 400 `request-rejected` with `code` `INVALID_LEAGUE`, an unknown
language 400 `INVALID_LANGUAGE`; the detail lists the valid values.

```json
{
  "total": 4000,
  "matching": 30,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 20,
  "rows": [
    {"rank": 1, "nickname": "Alice", "league": "Legend", "score": 50.1, "language": "C++",
     "country": "FR", "agent_id": 999, "percentage": 100, "me": true}
  ],
  "me": {"rank": 1, "nickname": "Alice", "...": "..."}
}
```

- `me` in a row: only on the user's row. The top-level `me` is the user's row wherever it is, absent
  when the user is not ranked.
- League bosses are not rows of this leaderboard: see `league_boss` in the progress.
- `agent_id`: the player's current agent. Test games only accept the agents of
  `GET /challenges/{public_id}/opponents`: players of higher leagues are refused.
- The leaderboard is cached for a short time; only its first 1000 matching rows can be paged through.

### GET /challenges/{public_id}/battles

Registered, started. Ranking games of one of the user's submissions, newest first, from every
league that submission played in.

| Query | Description |
|---|---|
| `submission` | A `submission_id` from `GET /submissions`, current or past. Default: the current submission. |
| `before` | Only games whose `game_id` is lower than this one: pass the `next_before` of the previous page. |
| `from` | Only games whose `game_id` is greater than or equal to this one. To fetch the games added or finished since a previous call, pass the lowest `game_id` that was `done` false then, or the highest `game_id` seen when none was: games do not end in `game_id` order. |
| `limit` | 1 to 100 (default 20). |

```json
{
  "submission_id": 321,
  "battles": [
    {"game_id": 123, "done": true, "ended_at": "2026-10-05T12:03:00Z", "my_position": 0,
     "players": [{"position": 0, "nickname": "Alice", "agent_id": 456, "me": true},
                 {"position": 1, "nickname": "Bronze boss", "agent_id": 789, "boss": true, "league": "Bronze"}]}
  ],
  "next_before": 123
}
```

- `next_before`: present when older games exist; absent on the last page. Page through all the games
  with `?before=<next_before>` until it is absent, keeping the same `from` if you sent one.
- `position` and `my_position` are 0 for the winner, absent while the game is being played (`done`
  false, no `ended_at`).
- `boss` and `league` are only on league bosses. A boss without nickname is named `<League> boss`.
- No `submission_id` and no battles when the user has no current submission and sent no `submission`.
- 404 `SUBMISSION_NOT_FOUND`: the submission is not one of the user's in this contest.
- No scores and no seeds here: they are in each game's log (`GET /games/{game_id}`).

items.text: The event starts on November 2nd at 10am CET and ends on November 9th at 10am CET. It starts at the same time for all players in the world, whatever the time zone.

items.text: Yes, you need to create a CodinGame account before being able to register for the challenge. We also suggest having a look at easy puzzles to get used to the platform.
items.title: Do I need a CodinGame account to compete?

items.text: By default, if you've added your company to your profile, depending on your rank, you'll contribute to your company for the company leaderboard. In the same way, if you've added your school to your profile, depending on your rank, you'll contribute points to your school for the school leaderboard. You can complete your profile here.
items.title: How can I compete for my school/company?

items.text: Only the top 100 schools and top 100 companies will be visible. Furthermore, it's possible to play the solo competition only.
items.title: I'm afraid of projecting a negative image of my school/company if I rank poorly. What can I do?

items.text: This is a bot programming (AI) challenge. New in bot programming? No worries, here's a guide for beginners.
items.title: What type of coding exercise should I expect?

items.text: We take the sum of points of the top 5 players in each company/school with at least 3 players. More info in this forum's thread.
items.title: How are the school/company leaderboards computed?

items.text: Copying code between players is forbidden during contests. We'll thoroughly monitor players' submissions and we reserve ourselves the right to ban any player in case of abuse.

contest_api_invitation:
Welcome to a quick edition of this year's Fall challenge! This time, we have selected to put the spotlight on an existing community game.

This challenge will be the chance for you to experiment with our new public API in a contest context. Whether you want to build your own submission framework, or orchestrate your agent directly, this API will allow you to submit and manage your submissions directly from new public enpoints.

Learn more about this API in your new API Tokens settings page.
